translationRepairs: Meng Mingyao retreated again and again, yet in the end he triumphed.
Meng Ming retreated again and again, yet in the end he triumphed.
s0029 names only 孟明; the original 'Meng Mingyao' invents a second syllable not in the sentence. The proposed 'Meng Ming' matches the source and remains natural English.
The dynasty tottered and may yet stand; the temples darkened and may yet see sacrifice again—only you and your brothers can carry the house of Sima through.
The altars of soil and grain tottered and may yet stand; the ancestral temples faded and may yet be continued—only you, enlightened lord, and your brothers can broadly rescue the royal plan.

The original invents 'house of Sima' and omits 明公 and 皇猷. The proposal restores those terms, but 'were in peril and may yet' mixes tenses and 'had been displaced' is an awkward gloss of 替. Keep the original hortatory cadence while rendering 社稷, 宗廟, 明公兄弟, and 弘濟皇猷.
When Yuan of Jin sent Gan Zhuo against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Sun Hui brought his troops in on Gan's side; Zhou Fu broke and ran.
When the Yuan Emperor sent Gan Zhuo against Zhou Fu at Shouyang, Sun Hui brought his troops in on Gan's side; Zhou Fu broke and ran.
元帝 is the Yuan Emperor. 'Yuan of Jin' is an unspecific and potentially misleading gloss; the proposed title is accurate.
He Rui of Lujiang held the Anfeng magistracy while Sun Hui kept a temporary hold on the district.
He Rui of Lujiang was Grand Administrator of Anfeng, while Sun Hui kept a temporary hold on the commandery borders.
太守 is the commandery Grand Administrator, not a county magistracy, and 郡境 is the commandery borders, not a vague 'district'.
His grandfather Xiong Qiao had once served Shi Chong as a household steward, yet remained honest and carried himself like a gentleman.
His grandfather Xiong Qiao had once served Shi Chong as a bondservant, yet remained honest and carried himself like a gentleman.
蒼頭 denotes a menial or bondservant. 'Household steward' inflates the office; the following 免之 (manumission) confirms servile status.
Yuan of Jin took his advice.
元帝納之 is the Yuan Emperor accepting the advice. 'Yuan of Jin' collides with the biographical subject 熊遠.
Xiong Yuan impeached Diao Xie and stripped him of his post.
Xiong Yuan impeached Diao Xie and had him dismissed from office.
奏免 is impeachment that results in dismissal, not Yuan himself stripping the office. The proposed agency is correct.
Duke Huan of Qi gave up meat and wine for seven years after a defeat; today's shame runs deeper still.
The Marquis of Qi gave up meat and wine for seven years after a defeat; today's shame runs deeper still.
The sentence names only 齊侯. Identifying him as Duke Huan is an unstated historical gloss.
When Gu Yi wrote bluntly, Emperor Wu made him magistrate of Tunliu and opened remonstrance posts so straight words had a door—men could speak their minds without fear.
When Guo Yi wrote bluntly, Emperor Wu made him magistrate of Tunliu and opened remonstrance posts so straight words had a door—men could speak their minds without fear.
郭翼 romanizes as Guo Yi; Gu Yi misreads 郭.

Gu Yi submitted a memorial, and Emperor Wu promoted him to magistrate of Tunliu; moreover he set up remonstrance officials in order to accept straight speech and draw forward the future, therefore each man could exhaust himself and words had no hidden reserve.

Guo Yi submitted a memorial, and Emperor Wu promoted him to magistrate of Tunliu; moreover he set up remonstrance officials in order to accept straight speech and draw forward the future, therefore each man could exhaust himself and words had no hidden reserve.
The same 郭翼 error appears in the literal field; Guo Yi is the correct romanization.
Yao drew Shun from obscurity, Shun from mountain caves; the Duke of Zhou did not bend law for kin, nor Shu Xiang for a brother's son.
Yao drew Shun from obscurity, Shun from mountain caves; the Duke of Zhou did not bend law for kin, nor Shu Xiang for his brothers.
孔懷 is the Shijing kenning for brothers, not a brother's son. The proposal restores that kinship.
His younger brother Xiong Jin, less famous but still able, served Wang Dun as chief clerk and died as grand administrator of Poyang.
His younger brother Xiong Jin, less famous but still able, served Wang Dun as recorder and ended as grand administrator of Poyang.
主簿 is recorder, distinct from 長史 in the previous sentence, and 終於 marks the terminal post, not death.
His father Wang Jun had been palace secretary.
His father Wang Jun had been palace aide to the censor-in-chief.
御史中丞 is palace aide to the censor-in-chief, not a palace secretary.
Once Marquis Shen of Qi feared his army was growing old before battle was joined; how much more now, after three years in armor with lice in the mail—can we not think deeply!
Once, while the Qi army had not yet reached its term, Marquis Shen feared it was growing old; how much more now, after three years in armor with lice in the mail—can we not think deeply!
齊旅 is the Qi army and 申侯 is Marquis Shen; the original wrongly makes Shen a Qi marquis and drops the army as subject.
When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and later even petty favors hid behind that code.
When Sima Lun seized the throne, the three princes issued the 《Yihai Precedent》 to rank wartime merit, and afterward even small merit awards all continued to use that code.
其後論功雖小，亦皆依用 means later merit assessments, even small ones, all followed the Yihai Precedent. 'Petty favors hid behind that code' is invented.
This was in itself a law for all cases, not a norm for ordinary categories.
This was itself an expedient one-time law, not a standard for ordinary categories.
一切之法 here is an ad hoc expedient, set against 非常倫之格, not a statute covering all cases.
Men like Ma Long and Meng Guan rose from nothing to great deeds, yet war was not their craft and they seldom lasted.
Men like Ma Long and Meng Guan rose from poverty to great deeds, yet because commanding armies was not what they had practiced, they were rarely able to succeed.
以所不習而統戎事，鮮能以濟 means they were rarely able to succeed at command they had not practiced, not that they seldom lasted.

The Yuan Emperor praised him and pardoned him, appointed him adviser, and he then passed through eminent posts to grand administrator of Danyang, grand master of splendid happiness, and was enfeoffed as count of Jianchang.

The Yuan Emperor praised him and pardoned him, appointed him adviser, and he then passed through eminent posts to governor of Danyang, grand master of splendid happiness, and was enfeoffed as count of Jianchang.
丹陽尹 is the capital-area yin/governor, not commandery 太守.
When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he brought him in as marshal to the army that soothes the ruler.
When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he brought him in as marshal of the pacification army.
撫軍司馬 is Sima of the Pacification Army, not 'the army that soothes the ruler'.
You serve in the field and I in the chamber, yet we both exist to save the dynasty and the house of Sima.
You serve in the field and I in the chamber, yet we both exist to save the altars of the state and to protect house and country.
安社稷，保家國 is altars of the state and house-and-country. 'House of Sima' is not in the Chinese.

Gao Song's letter to Huan Wen and Chen Yun's stand against Xie Jie broke reckless mobilization, revived the Run-Ying argument, echoed Guo Jia's bluntness and Zhu Yu's wit—so Huan Wen dropped a rash Xun You scheme and Xie Jie learned to admire Wang Lang's example.

Gao Song's letter to Huan Wen and Chen Yun's stand against Xie Jie broke reckless mobilization, revived the Run-Ying argument, echoed Guo Jia's bluntness and Zhu Yu's wit—so Huan Wen dropped a rash Xu You scheme and Xie Jie learned to admire Wang Lang's example.
許攸 is Xu You; Xun You would be 荀攸.
He fled Chengdu under an alias and moved Sima Yue with his pen.
He fled Ying under an alias and moved Yue with his pen.
違穎 is departing Ying, not Chengdu; 幹越 is lobbying Yue. The original place-name is false.

元帝 is captured as a local ruler but the packet has no reign table, so the Shouyang campaign year is unresolved.
陛下 is the reigning Jin emperor addressed in the memorial; owned units give no personal name.
二帝 are two unburied emperors; they are not named in this chunk and are not individuated beyond the dual count.
齊侯 is not given a personal name in the Chinese; English Duke Huan is not source-backed.
武帝 is not identified beyond the posthumous title in this chunk.
夏侯/Xiahou is a surname-only opponent of Liu Bei at Hanshan; the chapter does not identify which Xiahou.
The Prince of Pei is titled only as 沛王; which prince is not identified.
元禮 is a courtesy name without a surname in this chapter.
The emperor of the inheritance edict is unnamed beyond 帝.
Zhang Liang, the Xiang house / Xiang Yu, and the Duke of Pei / Liu Bang are dated only as 昔; Western years need independent late Qin–early Han mapping.
Sun Hui, the Prince of Qi / Sima Jiong, and the Prince of the Eastern Sea / Sima Yue lack packet reign mapping for their Western Jin activity.
Guo Jia, Zhu Yu, Xu You (許攸; English Xun You), and Wang Lang are comparative exemplars without packet chronology for their own lives.
